title: prewarm-chunk-orchestrator-and-decode-concurrency-adapter
author: Asha Patel
commit_summary: a1f3d9c: introduce PrewarmChunkOrchestrator with adaptive chunk sizing and ttl-aware enqueue
b2e4f0a: add DecodingConcurrencyAdapter to surface decode backpressure and suggested prewarm rate
c3d5a12: wire metrics and dashboard hooks, add unit tests and example, docs and benchmarks
description: Context: we observe tail-latency and cost variance when the prefill (token priming) stage either over-primes (wasting KV cache fills) or under-primes (starving decode kernels). This PR introduces a lightweight prewarm orchestration layer and a decode-side concurrency adapter to reduce oscillation between prefill and decode stages while improving KV cache coherence. Motivation: reduce p95/p99 token latency and smooth GPU kernel scheduling by aligning prefill chunk size and pacing with observed decode consumption and KV hit efficiency. This is complementary to existing speculative and chunked prefill work but approaches the problem from an orchestration + feedback perspective rather than low-level kernel fusion. What changed: - PrewarmChunkOrchestrator (services/serving/scheduler/prewarm_orchestrator.py): groups incoming prefill requests into adaptive-sized chunks based on a sliding window of recent KV hit-rate, sequence length distribution, and decode concurrency hints. Uses a configurable hysteresis to avoid rapid chunk-size oscillation. - DecodingConcurrencyAdapter (services/serving/scheduler/decoding_concurrency_adapter.py): decode stage publishes a small set of runtime indicators (active_decode_slots, avg_decode_runtime_ms, preferred_prefill_batch) which the orchestrator consumes to modulate prewarm pacing. - KV cache integration (runtime/kv_cache/*): new metrics exported (kv_prefill_hits, kv_prefill_evictions, kv_prefill_latency) and a minor eviction-policy tweak to prefer retaining keys for actively decoding shards. - Metrics & observability: added dashboard hooks and tracing annotations for prewarm lifecycle, chunk boundary events, and decode backpressure signals. - Tests & benchmarks: unit tests for orchestrator and adapter, benchmark harness config and comparison run showing 7-12% improvement on p95 for interactive chat traces at medium concurrency, and 4-6% token cost reduction due to higher KV reuse. - Docs & examples: ops doc describing tuning knobs and an example script demonstrating prewarm enrollment. Checklist: - [x] Implement orchestrator and adapter - [x] Unit tests for orchestrator and adapter - [x] KV metrics and small eviction tweak - [x] Benchmark config and run - [x] Docs and examples - [x] CI green (flaky test addressed) Backwards compatibility and rollout: default behavior is opt-in via a feature flag (SERVING_PREWARM_V2). On by default for dedicated clusters in canary for 2 weeks before global rollout. No changes to public API surface. Related: follows up on ENG-6123 study into prefill inefficiencies and is intentionally orthogonal to kernel-fusion efforts (see ENG-7901). Performance notes: aggregated benchmark (benchmarks/prefill_vs_decode/2026-02-25-prewarm-bench.yaml) indicates consistent p95 reductions on small/medium sequence mixes when KV hit-rate is above 18%. Edge cases: when KV hit-rate is very low the orchestrator reduces chunking aggressiveness and falls back to single-request prefill to avoid wasted work. Implementation detail summary: the orchestrator uses a token-bucket-esque pacing loop and groups requests up to a configurable max_chunk_tokens. The adapter subscribes on the internal event bus; to keep the critical path small the adapter only sends +- integer suggestions (increase/decrease) rather than full histograms. See docs/ops/prewarm_and_decode.md for tuning guidance.
review_comments: Luca Romano: Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: (1) can we add a small end-to-end integration test that simulates a decode slowdown to validate the backpressure loop? (2) the hysteresis constants look aggressive; please parameterize them and add defaults tuned to 95th percentile workloads.

Asha Patel: Added a synthetic e2e test (runtime/tests/test_prewarm_orchestrator.py) that simulates decode slot starvation and asserts orchestrator backs off within 200ms. Hysteresis constants are now configuration fields with conservative defaults; documented in docs/ops/prewarm_and_decode.md.
Priya Menon: I saw a local failure on test_kv_eviction_policy showing timing sensitivity. Can you stabilize that test?
Asha Patel: Fixed by switching that test to use deterministic clock advance and increased the eviction grace window in policy.py; added a comment explaining the time-coupling. Re-ran CI.
Samir Gulati: Metrics look good. One nit: the dashboard panels should expose kv_prefill_hits as a rate not a counter. I left a small suggestion in the dashboard yaml. Approving after CI is green.
Priya Menon: Approve (looks reasonable; bench shows clear improvement).
